mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the Registrar of Companies; authenticated by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs by apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention. No consular legalization is required or permitted in parallel.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarised by a New Zealand notary public; subsequent apostille by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs under the Hague Apostille Convention. Consular legalization is not applicable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarised by a New Zealand notary public; subsequent apostille by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs under the Hague Apostille Convention. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the bank; if required by the destination jurisdiction, notarised by a New Zealand notary public and then apostilled by the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs under the Hague Apostille Convention. Consular legalization is not undertaken for Apostille Convention members.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening against the New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List and autonomous sanctions, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, and the consolidated sanctions lists of the United Kingdom and the European Union. The AML/CFT programme must also include FATF high-risk jurisdiction monitoring, Interpol notices, global PEP databases, adverse-media screening, source-of-wealth/source-of-funds verification, 25% beneficial-ownership identification, annual re-screening, and continuous transaction monitoring for escrow deposits and wire transfers in the immigration advisory business.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - New Zealand Companies Register online name approval and reservation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be in English or te reo Maori (including macron diacritics). Non-English/non-Maori names require an English or Maori transliteration/translation. The four-tier naming convention applies: (1) exact name search; (2) phonetic-equivalence check; (3) translated-equivalence check; and (4) alphanumeric and special-character normalisation. Names must not be offensive, misleading, or identical/confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of a rejection notice, the applicant may request reconsideration in writing from the Registrar of Companies, stating the proposal, the legal ground of objection, and any evidence that the name is not confusingly similar. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review under the Companies Act 1993. The letter must be supplied with certified copies and payment of the applicable filing fee. A new name application may be filed without waiting for the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox may satisfy the minimum registered-office address condition of the Companies Act 1993 only if it is a physical street address in New Zealand at which service can be effected. However, a virtual office is not acceptable as the principal place of business for an immigration-visa advisory company required to be licensed under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007, and New Zealand banks will ordinarily reject a pure commercial-mailbox address for corporate account opening because AML/CFT customer due diligence requires verifiable physical business premises, client-meeting capacity, and operational substance. Inland Revenue may also reject a mailbox only address for GST registration absent evidence of genuine economic activity. Therefore, for this industry, a virtual office is not recommended and is treated as high-risk if used.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced visits: physical signage, active tenancy agreement, staff present, client files and AML/CFT programme manual, board minute book, statutory registers, and transaction records. Quantified risk: low-to-moderate for the New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue, estimated at 10-15% during the first 18 months; elevated for the Immigration Advisers Authority if a licence is held, with an estimated 25-30% likelihood of a compliance inspection in the first licensing year. Unannounced on-site checks are possible but more common only where unrelated party transactions, escrow payments, or high-risk foreign-citizen client flows are detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand, particularly sections 12 to 15 on registration, section 16 on the constitution, section 25 on capacity, section 128 on board authority, section 153 on issuing shares, section 189 on the registered office, and related provisions of the Companies (Incorporation and Consequential Amendments) Regulations 2023; the Financial Services Legislation Amendment Act imposes supplementary obligations only if regulated financial services are offered, which is not the case here.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company under the Companies Act 1993, submitted electronically through the Companies Office online incorporation system, together with the company constitution, consent to act forms, and shareholder vigilancy declarations if applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up share capital is required under New Zealand law; there is no blocked escrow capital account and no capital deposit threshold. The board may authorise shares to be issued for cash, property or services, and shares must either be fully paid or lawfully designated as unpaid with a call requirement recorded in the share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION IN THE MATTER OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 OF NEW ZEALAND AND IN THE MATTER OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED. The persons whose names appear as the first directors of [COMPANY NAME] Limited, a company incorporated on [DATE] under the Companies Act 1993, hereby convene the inaugural meeting by unanimous written consent and unanimously resolve as follows. 1. The constitution adopted on incorporation is ratified in full and the company adopts the registered office at [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], New Zealand. The board instructs the company secretary or any director to file any change of registered office with the Companies Office in accordance with section 189 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. The initial subscription for ordinary shares by the founding shareholders, as recorded in the share register, is approved and ratified. The board is authorised to issue, allot and establish the consideration for further shares, and to receive payment for such shares, provided that the requirements of the Companies Act 1993 and the company constitution are satisfied. 3. The board appoints [BANK NAME] New Zealand Limited, or such other registered New Zealand bank as the directors may select, as the banker of the company. The directors are authorised to open operating accounts, escrow accounts and client trust accounts for the study-abroad and immigration visa advisory business, and any two directors or one director together with the company secretary may sign cheques, wire transfer instructions, internet banking authorities and all related banking documents. 4. The following statutory officers are appointed: [NAME] as Chairperson, [NAME] as Managing Director, [NAME] as Company Secretary, and [NAME] as Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Compliance Officer, each to serve until the first annual shareholders meeting unless earlier replaced by board resolution. 5. The company adopts the use of a ring-fenced escrow or client trust account for all client funds relating to immigration applications and student placements, so that no client funds are commingled with operating funds. 6. The directors and officers are authorised to execute all statutory forms, bank mandates, licence applications and professional engagement documents necessary to commence lawful business operations. This resolution is effective as of the date of incorporation and may be relied upon by financial institutions, regulatory authorities and third parties without further board action. CERTIFIED by the Chairperson on [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and entity profile design
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, through the NZBN and Companies Register online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a real-time name search and availability check on the Companies Office register to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and that it terminates with Limited or Ltd as approved. Confirm that the proposed name does not contain restricted words requiring business or ministerial consent, and that the ISIC 7810 study-abroad and immigration advisory scope is reflected accurately in the company objects if a bespoke constitution is adopted. Prepare the constitutional share structure, identify the true beneficial owners, and reserve the company name in the online portal. Obtain a formal memorandum identifying the AML/CFT medium-risk profile and the intended use of escrow and wire transfer payment rails.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and at least two alternate names
Full legal names, residential addresses, dates of birth and proof of identity for each proposed director
Details of proposed shareholders and intended shareholding percentages
Draft constitution or express election to adopt the Companies Act default constitution
Statement of principal business purpose referencing ISIC 7810 and NAICS 541199
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, promptly file a new name application with alternate names and provide written reasons; internally request reconsideration by the Companies Office registrar, and if the refusal rests on restricted wording, provide consent from the issuing ministry or select a non-restricted name before incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory incorporation filing with the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, online through the Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation application in the Companies Office online portal, entering the reserved company name, physical registered office address, address for service, share structure, director and shareholder details, and the constitution if a bespoke constitution is adopted. Ensure every founding director signs and submits the prescribed consent to act as director form and acknowledges the statutory duties under the Companies Act 1993, including the duties to act in good faith, to exercise reasonable care and diligence, and to avoid conflicts of interest. Provide certified proof of identity for each director and beneficial owner, and make the statutory declaration that the company is being formed for a lawful purpose and will not be engaged in prohibited immigration practices. The registrar will issue the certificate of incorporation and the company will automatically receive a New Zealand Business Number.
required_dossiers: Completed Companies Office online incorporation application
Company constitution executed in writing, or statutory default election
Consent to act as director executed by each proposed director
Certified passports or national identity cards for directors and shareholders
Proof of residential address dated within the prior six months for each director
Register of directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the flagged fields in the online application and resubmit within fifteen business days with explanatory evidence. If the Registrar suspends or rejects the incorporation, file written submissions and corrected documentation, and if the rejection is not resolved, seek internal review and thereafter judicial review before the High Court of New Zealand.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue registration and bank account activation with escrow capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand and the appointing New Zealand registered trading bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated company with the IRD for income tax and obtain an IRD number; if taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in rolling turnover, apply for goods and services tax registration in the same online portal. Use the certificate of incorporation, NZBN certificate, and board resolution to open a corporate operating bank account and a separate escrow or client trust account for study abroad and immigration visa fees. The bank will perform enhanced customer due diligence on all legal and beneficial owners and will require evidence of the AML/CFT risk rating and the source of funds. Execute bank mandates consistent with the first board resolution, and establish a policy that client funds are held in the dedicated escrow account and are only released upon service delivery milestones or regulatory approval.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by the Companies Office
NZBN registration certificate
Board resolution authorising account opening and signatories
IRD registration application or completed Inland Revenue tax file application
AML/CFT bank questionnaire for beneficial owners
Source of entity funds and proof of lawful origin
Professional indemnity insurance certificate if required by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD delays the issuance of an IRD number, escalate to the IRD Business Integrity team by written request and request urgent allocation under the applicable tax administration protocol. If the bank declines or queries the application due to AML concerns, update the ownership and source of funds documentation, rescale the risk rating, or select another registered New Zealand bank; interim client payments may be held in a solicitor or licensed immigration adviser trust account only if the Code of Conduct permits such holding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Immigration adviser licensing and study-abroad regulatory authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Immigration Advisers Authority (IAA), a unit of the New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, together with the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA) for international education agent signatory requirements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether any person in the company will provide immigration advice as defined by the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007. If so, at least one licensed individual must hold a current New Zealand immigration adviser licence of the appropriate class before services are offered. Submit the prescribed application to the IAA with evidence of the adviser qualification, English proficiency, character and fitness, professional indemnity insurance, and a client money and escrow management plan. For student placement services to New Zealand education institutions, execute the applicable NZQA signatory undertaking or enter into a written sub-agent agreement with a licensed International Student Recruitment agent if direct signatory status is not yet obtained. All advertisements, contracts and invoicing must state the licence number or the exempt legal practitioner status. A formal written policy must be adopted prohibiting unlicensed persons from giving immigration advice.
required_dossiers: IAA online application for immigration adviser licence
Evidence of recognised qualification and adviser assessment
Police clearance certificates from every country of residence over the prior ten years
Character reference letters and disclosure of any pending disciplinary matters
Professional indemnity insurance certificate
Escrow or client trust account plan and sample client agreement
NZQA signatory undertaking or authorised sub-agent agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IAA declines an application, request full written reasons, exercise the internal reconsideration mechanism within the statutory time frame, and appeal any negative decision to the Immigration Advisers Tribunal. The company must not market itself as licensed while an appeal is pending, and it may instead operate through a supervisor who holds an appropriate licence until the appeal is determined.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT compliance programme, privacy governance, and final operational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) AML/CFT Group, together with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner under the Privacy Act 2020 and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit for suspicious activity reporting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint the AML/CFT compliance officer and approve a written risk-based compliance programme before onboarding clients. Determine whether the company meets the definition of a reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; if the company is a reporting entity, register the programme with the Department of Internal Affairs and file annual compliance audits if required. Institute customer due diligence procedures, enhanced due diligence for medium-risk clients, politically exposed person screening, source of funds verification, transaction monitoring, and a suspicious transaction report workflow to the Financial Intelligence Unit. Appoint a privacy officer and adopt a Privacy Act 2020 policy, data retention schedule, and digital security plan. All escrow and wire transfers must be matched against client engagement letters, and whistle-blower and anti-corruption policies must be distributed to staff.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT risk assessment and business risk profile
AML/CFT written compliance programme
Customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence templates
Politically exposed person and sanctions screening policy
Suspicious transaction reporting procedure
Privacy Act 2020 privacy policy and data breach response plan
Information security policy for digital client files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIA requests corrective action, submit a comprehensive remediation plan within twenty working days, retain an experienced AML/CFT compliance consultant to revise the programme, and voluntarily cease onboarding new clients only if an immediate risk of criminal misuse is identified. If the Privacy Commissioner raises concerns, amend the data gathering practices and issue a corrective action notice to all staff to prevent regulatory enforcement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – the entity operates exclusively as a professional advisory and immigration visa consulting service under ISIC 7810 / NAICS 541199, with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, processing or warehousing activities; therefore no industrial licensing authority is engaged.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Immigration Adviser Licence under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007, and where applicable, NZQA International Education Agent signatory registration or authorised sub-agent approval for recruitment of international students.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Environment and Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand – registration not applicable for a service-only activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Not Applicable under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the National Environmental Standards; this purely advisory and placement business does not trigger any mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment, resource consent, designated activity, or Full EIA Report threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; there are no wastewater discharges, VOC emissions, hazardous waste streams, particulate air emissions, or chemical storage volumes. General office waste is managed by municipal refuse collection, and digital-only client dossiers produce no regulated physical effluents. If future office fit-out occurs, the landlord/tenant must comply with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality only if combustion appliances are installed, which is not the case here.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for manufacturing or chemical operations because there is no physical industrial plant. As a low-risk advisory office, the business must nevertheless hold a valid Building Warrant of Fitness where the Building Act 2004 compliance schedule applies to means of escape from fire, maintain a Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 worker safety system with fire extinguishers, first aid kit, emergency evacuation plan, and a traffic control plan only if a dedicated waiting area of more than ten persons is used. No Civil Defense fire permit is required for a professional office, and an emergency evacuation procedure must be registered with the local fire and emergency authority if the landlord requires it.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), the national revenue authority of New Zealand, operating the myIR online portal at https://www.ird.govt.nz/myir. New Zealand tax filings, GST registrations, and IRD number administration are all processed through this statutory body.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited company must obtain an IRD number (the statutory tax identification number for income tax, GST, PAYE, and FBT) by: (1) undertaking the Companies Office New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registration if the entity is incorporated in New Zealand or, for offshore entities, registering the foreign company on the national companies register under the Companies Act 1993 if it carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand; (2) filing the Inland Revenue non-resident company tax registration application either online through myIR or through an approved tax agent, supplying certified certificate of incorporation, registered address in New Zealand, directors' names, foreign tax residence details, and the date New Zealand taxable activity commences; (3) upon IRD acceptance, receiving a unique IRD number for filing corporate income tax returns, GST returns, and employer obligations; (4) separately activating GST registration in myIR once the NZD 60,000 taxable-supply threshold is exceeded or where the entity voluntarily elects registration; and (5) maintaining the IRD number as the primary TIN while procuring a customs client code from the New Zealand Customs Service for any physical export transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand has no US-style check-the-box election. A limited company is taxed as a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act 2007. Eligible closely held companies with no more than five qualifying shareholders may elect look-through company (LTC) treatment to be fiscally transparent. Additional statutory elections include group tax consolidation under subpart IG, GST grouping under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, and available hybrid entity mismatch adjustments under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018, which are not elective waivers but mandatory override rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) imposed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 on broad-based consumption in New Zealand.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; once this economic turnover threshold is exceeded, GST registration is compulsory. Voluntary registration below the threshold is available for businesses carrying on a taxable activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or supply-chain e-invoicing approval. Inland Revenue supports voluntary Peppol BIS 3.0-based e-invoicing through the A-NZ network; traditional paper and PDF tax invoices remain legally valid. GST-registered suppliers must issue a tax invoice for every taxable supply exceeding NZD 50 (excluding GST), and retain full records for seven years. GST returns are filed electronically in myIR with no API-based pre-clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for zero-rating under section 11 of the GST Act 1985 where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand by contractual arrangement and ownership passes to a non-resident before departure. Services, including study-abroad placement and immigration visa advisory, qualify for zero-rating under section 11A when the services are supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided they are not supplied directly in connection with New Zealand land, New Zealand moveable personal property, or supplied to an associated person physically present in New Zealand. The supplier must hold written evidence of the non-resident status, the offshore location of the recipient, and the source of the payment to satisfy Revenue audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or House Air Waybill (if any physical shipment accompanies the service)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reopen historical GST returns and assess unrecovered GST where zero-rating is not substantiated; the statutory non-evasion time bar is four years and evasion has no time bar. Clawback includes the previously zero-rated output tax re-grossed at 15%, use-of-money interest from the original due date, and TAA shortfall penalties: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for fraudulent or wilful evasion. Fraudulent claims can also attract criminal conviction penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994, with separate exposure for misleading Customs documentation under the Customs and Excise Act 2018.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ), acting jointly with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as the AML/CFT supervisor for registered financial service providers
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised convertible currency regime. Both current account and capital account transactions are freely permitted with no general exchange control approvals, pre-notification, or mandatory foreign exchange surrender requirements. Profit remittances and repatriation of investment proceeds are unrestricted; the sole practical hurdles are standard corporate tax compliance, director verification, and bank-level AML/CFT source-of-funds due diligence. Non-resident investment is facilitated through standard share capital or shareholder loan structures; the only regulatory overlay is the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which applies to specific sensitive land and significant business assets, not to ordinary treasury flows of a study-abroad and immigration advisory company.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or obligatory surrender ratio for export receipts in New Zealand. The RBNZ does not require conversion of foreign currency earnings into NZD, and no minimum export proceeds retention threshold applies. An NZ LTD may invoice, receive, hold, and disburse foreign currency freely. However, all foreign-sourced income and foreign currency gains must be declared for New Zealand income tax purposes, and bank transfers referencing consultancy services must be supported by properly executed service agreements and tax invoices to satisfy AML/CFT record-keeping.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium viability as primary treasury infrastructure. Offshore digital EMI providers are not licensed banks in New Zealand and cannot directly access local clearing systems such as Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) or acquire RBNZ settlement accounts. Their use should be limited to ancillary receivables collection or pre-payment facilitation for overseas students, and only if the EMI is registered on the FMA AML/CFT supervised entity register and meets New Zealand data-residency and consumer-protection standards. The principal operating entity in New Zealand must maintain at least one physical corporate account with a locally incorporated licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors is not statutorily mandatory in New Zealand. Registered banks permitted electronic remote onboarding under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, provided that customer identification is conducted using acceptable electronic verification methods. In practice, Tier 1 banks generally require a live video call interview with the director or beneficial owner, notarised company documents, certified passport and proof-of-address copies, and a completed AML/CFT questionnaire for an immigration/visa consultancy entity. A physical branch visit is rarely required, but the bank may request apostilled corporate registers and legal opinions from the jurisdiction of incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business classification due to immigration and visa advisory services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current immigration adviser licence or exemption certificate issued by the Immigration Advisers Authority; detailed service-level agreement separating advisory fees from university tuition disbursement; written AML/CFT compliance programme under the responsible NZ reporting entity; client acceptance policy for non-resident students; evidence of qualifications and professional indemnity insurance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Front-of-house fundflows involving upfront student payments from unrelated third parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sworn declarations from each student; contractual vacation of refund rights; bank statements of the student for last six months verifying source of funds; passport and visa copies; proof of relationship to the paying party; academic admission letters from the relevant New Zealand educational institution; third-party payment authorisation forms notarised or certified by a lawyer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque ownership chain with non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full company registry extract, overseas corporate register certificate, share register, trust deed or shareholder agreement, ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, personal identification of every 25% owner, and a tax-residency confirmation from the shareholder's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons among students or sponsors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP identification at onboarding; written source-of-wealth statement covering employment history, business activity and accumulated assets; supporting audited financial statements, bank reference letters, tax return summaries, and legal documents evidencing the legitimacy of the wealth; ongoing enhanced transaction monitoring and senior-manager approval of deposits above the prescribed threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions contingent on immigration outcomes or visa approval
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated escrow account structure with clear disbursement trigger conditions; formal immigration-advice engagement contract; refund and penalty mechanisms; school partnership agreements; signed acknowledgment that visa approval cannot be guaranteed; evidence that fee is for professional advisory time rather than for immigration outcome.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections from non-resident shareholders should be remitted by SWIFT MT103 to the NZ corporate account using the principal bank's BIC and the corporate account IBAN. The remittance instruction must identify the purpose as either 'Equity Investment - New Zealand Limited Company' or 'Shareholder Subordinated Loan' as applicable. The commercial contract, board resolution, and registered bank's source-of-funds questionnaire must be filed in the bank's KYC package. Because New Zealand has no central bank exchange-control approval, the only gateways are bank-level AML/CFT checks and, where relevant, the Overseas Investment Commission consent process for sensitive asset investment; for a service-sector study-abroad consulting entity, no OIA consent is ordinarily required. The bank may require a lawyer's letter of opinion and a completed CRS self-certification before activating inward remittance credits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements to educational institutions and overseas service partners should be effected through tested correspondent banking rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct credit transfers for tuition payments, accommodation bookings, insurance premiums, and settlement of advisory-invoice invoices; (ii) Commercial documentary letters of credit opened through the NZ issuing bank under UCP 600, using SWIFT MT700, for high-value or deferred-payment arrangements with overseas education groups; (iii) inbound or domestic escrow instructions for client trust balances held pending disbursement trigger approvals. All outbound raws must carry detailed purpose codes as specified by the destination clearing system, include the receiving institution's bank verification certificate, and be supported by underlying contracts, tax invoices, and student acknowledgment forms to avoid AML/CFT friction at the beneficiary's corresponding bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable New Zealand dollar forwards with licensed local banks and registered swap dealers
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies in which active local NZD deliverable markets are absent, subject to bank credit approval
Plain vanila FX options and currency swaps for managing tuition-fee and consulting-receivable currency mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps where a fixed-rate student payment receivable is used to service a floating-rate funding facility
FX-swap structures combining spot conversion with an agreed forward re-exchange schedule

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Companies Act 1993
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the annual return date, which is the anniversary of incorporation unless otherwise fixed by the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty imposed by the Registrar; public company status marked 'Overdue Annual Return'; persistent failure permits removal from the New Zealand Register after formal notice and Gazette advertisement, with reinstatement requiring court order or Registrar consent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for most private NZ limited companies; compulsory audit applies if the company meets the Financial Reporting Act 2013 'large' entity thresholds (total assets > NZ$60 million, total revenue > NZ$30 million, or more than 100 employees), or if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS / NZ GAAP); eligible entities may apply the reduced disclosure regime (NZ IFRS RDR).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate annual UBO filing. The Annual Return requires confirmation of current directors and shareholding details; share transfers during the year must be reflected in the company's own share register, and the Companies Office record must be updated by the next Annual Return. AML/CFT client due diligence obligations continue to require maintained beneficial-owner records for the immigration visa advisory business.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Books of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–12,000 for a typical small to medium advisory company, when an audit is required or requested

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand imposes a flat 28% corporate income tax rate with no general statutory tax holidays. The Imputation Credit System eliminates economic double taxation of distributed profits. Eligible R&D activities qualify for a 15% tax credit (R&D Loss Tax Credit regime effective from 2022-23 income year). No preferential rate for immigration advisory businesses; foreign-owned companies are subject to the same rate. Non-resident companies are taxed on New Zealand-sourced income only.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed via Inland Revenue's myIR secure online portal; approved tax agents may file via E-File or XML gateway.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: IR4 terminal tax and filing deadline is generally 7 February following the balance date for a 31 March standard balance date; the due date may be extended to 7 April for non-standard balance dates. Provisional tax payments are due in three instalments (or two for ratio/estimation method).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income from all sources derived in New Zealand and overseas (attributable under the CFC rules if applicable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies report only New Zealand-sourced income; specify exclusions separately and attach a schedule of offshore services revenue not taxable under New Zealand law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from a New Zealand business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include fees for immigration consulting and student placement advisory services where the source is New Zealand (services performed in New Zealand or contract negotiated/implemented in New Zealand).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, dividends and other investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies declare gross interest and dividends sourced in New Zealand; subject to non-resident withholding tax unless in a portfolio investment or exempt category is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident contractors' income or withholding income (if applicable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert amounts subject to withholding tax paid under PAYE or approved issuer levy; attach certificates of withholding.

Claim directly related deductible expenditures: salaries, rent, professional indemnity insurance, marketing, regulatory licensing fees, depreciation. Do not deduct head-office cost allocations unless supported by an apportionment methodology; non-resident companies must apply limitation under section DN 5 for head office expenditure in excess of arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable income or taxable loss before imputation credits (taxable profit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate as total income minus allowable expenses; loss companies must complete loss carry-forward schedules in Box 17.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income at 28%; account for imputation credits attached by any dividend received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company computes 28% tax on net taxable income; foreign tax credits (Box 20) are limited to New Zealand tax attributable to that foreign source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss offsets and loss carry-forward information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company can carry forward New Zealand tax losses only if continuous shareholder continuity of 49% or more is maintained; the 2020-21 to 2022-23 temporary loss carry-back provision (now expired) is not available after the 2023-24 income year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account details and elections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are not required to maintain an imputation credit account unless they have elected to attach imputation credits to dividends; if no account is maintained, dividends paid are subject to further withholding tax at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach annual shareholders' remuneration declaration and director's certificate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all director remuneration and payments made to associated non-resident enterprises; director exposure to personal liability requires a signed declaration that the information is true and correct.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: initial penalty NZD 50 per month (capped at NZD 100 for small companies) or NZD 250 per month for companies (capped at NZD 2,500). An additional 2.5% arrears penalty of unpaid tax applies on the day after the due date, plus a further 2.5% on day 7, 14 and 21 after the due date. Late payment interest (use-of-money interest) accrues daily at the prescribed rate (currently approximately 8.0-8.4% per annum on underpayments). Evasion penalties may reach 150% of the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory non-resident withholding tax on dividends is 30% for non-resident companies; the approved issuer levy (AIL) of 2% applies only in respect of interest paid on public securities issued by approved issuers, not dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the DTA, the foreign parent company must obtain an Inland Revenue certificate of residence (Form IR871 - Certificate of Residence) or the equivalent tax authority TRC from the home country, and provide it to the New Zealand company before the withholding tax is finalised or before filing the RWT/NRWT reconciliation to IRD. For jurisdictions qualifying as 'a fully developed double tax agreement', dividend withholding may be reduced to 5% if the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of the voting power; otherwise 15%. The payer must use IRD's NRWT rate selection process, maintain the TRC on file, and if the treaty rate is not applied at source, a refund claim via Form IR3NR or company refund application must be made. The new Zealand company must also determine if the non-resident shareholder is a 'fully developed DTA' resident and complete IRD form IR29 (RWT/NRWT reconciliation) to report the reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties is 15% and on interest 15%; the 2% approved issuer levy may apply to interest on securities of approved issuers. Under New Zealand's standard DTA network, royalty withholding is commonly reduced to 10% or 5% depending on the treaty; interest is generally reduced to 10% with some treaties providing 0% (e.g. Australia retains 10%, United Kingdom 10%, Japan 0% in some scenarios). The intellectual property royalties from a study-abroad or immigration agency's proprietary client-management software or franchise licensing fees are sourced to New Zealand if the IP is used in New Zealand. Withholding is not applicable to services fees unless recharacterised as royalty by the DTA. Royalty payments to foreign associated enterprises must also satisfy the transfer pricing arm's length requirement under section GC 6.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand's transfer pricing documentation thresholds: Local File is not mandatory for all taxpayers but the IRD requires contemporaneous documentation if the transaction value exceeds NZD 4 million for cross-border related-party transactions in a single income year; the Master File is expected where consolidated group revenue exceeds NZD 100 million and cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million. Administrative penalty provisions apply if documentation is not prepared and a tax shortfall arises from the transfer pricing adjustment.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand applies a robust economic substance doctrine through section GB 41 and GA 1 (general anti-avoidance). For immigration consulting companies, the IRD examines whether the New Zealand entity performs substantive functions: employment of local licensed advisers, physical office, local client contracts, and decision-making. A foreign-owned agency that merely routes study-abroad application fees or escrow funds to an offshore parent while claiming commission deductions without local substance will be recharacterised. New Zealand has adopted the OECD BEPS package; the transfer pricing rules in subpart GC apply to cross-border related-party arrangements, and the Arbitration Panel may allocate income based on economic substance. Dividends distributed from an enterprise lacking economic substance do not qualify for imputation credit refunds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excluding cash or online wire transfer/escrow fees from gross income, using shell companies to mischaracterise fees as exempt consultancy income, or creating artificial intercompany debt to strip profits from New Zealand services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, evasion penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall (s 141E); absolute discharge penalty of 200% for evasion with intent to conceal. Interest accrues. Criminal conviction for tax evasion under s 143A can result in a fine up to NZD 50,000 for an individual and NZD 250,000 for a company, and up to 5 years imprisonment for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for tax shortfalls if they have knowingly assisted in evasion or if they operated the company otherwise than in good faith (Companies Act 1993, s 300 and s 301). Courts may issue civil recovery orders, assets freezing orders, travel bans under the Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act, and extradition proceedings for serious tax evasion. Director disqualification under the Companies Act can last up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an NZ Ltd with no physical office, no employed licensed immigration advisers, no local engaged workforce, entirely offshore management, and using the New Zealand name merely to gain 'high-origin prestige' for visa and study abroad applications.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD may disregard the structure and attribute all New Zealand-sourced income to the foreign principal under the reconstruction provisions (s GA 1 and s GC 6). Penalties: shortfall penalty for unacceptable tax position (20%) or gross carelessness (40%). The Registrar of Companies may strike off the company under the Companies Act for not carrying on business; directors risk criminal liability for filing false statements under s 377.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell company can be personally liable for the company's debts if they allowed the business to operate while insolvent (s 135 reckless trading). The Financial Markets Authority or Immigration New Zealand may refer directors for fraudulent conduct in immigration services, causing cancellation of the company's immigration consulting licence and adverse immigration consequences for director visas.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an international student placement and Golden Visa residence advisory service without the required professional licence under the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act 2007, or knowingly facilitating visa applications through false information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to NZD 100,000 for unlicensed immigration advice (s 64 of the Immigration Advisers Licensing Act); a company that employs unlicensed advisers is subject to fines up to NZD 75,000 for each offence. Under the Immigration Act 2009, criminal liability for fraudulent documents carries imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine of up to NZD 100,000. Revenue derived from unlicensed activity is taxable as assessable income and cannot claim tax deductions for fines or penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, as persons concerned in the management, are jointly and severally liable for the fine if the offence is attributable to their consent, connivance or neglect. The Immigration Advisers Authority may impose a permanent ban on acting as an immigration adviser; personal travel bans and refusal of visas under section 157 Immigration Act may also apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling high-net-worth Golden Visa application fees, escrow funds, or tuition remittances without an Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance programme, failing to conduct customer due diligence, or moving funds through multiple foreign jurisdictions without suspicious transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AMLCFT Act), a company is subject to civil liability of up to NZD 2 million for each violation, and NZD 200,000 per violation for individuals. Criminal penalties for wilful or reckless breaches can reach imprisonment for up to 2 years. The FMA, Reserve Bank of New Zealand, and Department of Internal Affairs may suspend or cancel the reporting entity's AML registration, which functionally terminates the business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable if they were a party to the contravention or knowingly assisted in the breach. Individuals face imprisonment up to 2 years per offence in addition to fines. Directors of reporting entities must ensure an effective compliance programme and undergo AML training; AML enforcement action can result in statutory management, director banning orders, and extraterritorial travel bans under criminal mutual assistance mechanisms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying government officials or university admissions officers in overseas source countries to secure student placements or Golden Visa approvals, or making secret commissions to agents in violation of the Secret Commissions Act 1910.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Secret Commissions Act 1910 imposes a fine of up to NZD 20,000 for companies and imprisonment up to 2 years for individuals. The Crimes Act 1961 bribery provisions carry imprisonment up to 7 years and confiscation of proceeds. New Zealand ratified the OECD Anti-Bribery Convention; the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) may prosecute corporate offenders; any bribe-related payment is non-deductible and a criminal confiscation order under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1991 can recover assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised or knowingly permitted bribery face imprisonment up to 7 years. The director's conduct constitutes management breach under companies law, triggering personal liability for losses; travel bans and extradition are available to foreign anti-bribery authorities. A criminal conviction automatically disqualifies the director from managing a company for up to 10 years unless relief is granted by the Court.
